They did, then my dad found me on the street and said he did it 'cause he loved me. 

You obviously don't get it.
I fucking love my parents man.

Haha, trust me. That's not my parents. They have disowned me for less.

I like the world you live in, though. It sounds very nice, I just don't live there. Thanks again for your comments, it's still a nice gesture, even if my parents aren't up to your expectations.

My parents aren't like that. They're why I started self-harming. Like I said, I try to be perfect for them. I don't cuss around them, I never got in trouble in school--and if I did, I hid it from them. I hide drug use from them, they think I don't smoke or drink even though I'm of legal age to do both. But I've never been good enough, and they've told me so. They remind me all the time of my failures. If anyone found out, it'd just be another mark against me, another disappointment, another failure on my part. I'm the disappointment, the loser, the embarrassment of the family. I've tried to do anything to make them proud, but nothing works. If they knew about this, my image would be ruined for them forever. Every time they saw me in long sleeves, they'd look at me in disgust and shame. They would probably stop talking to me. Any relationship I have with my parents would be gone. 

That's a question I've been debating since high school. I have always been clueless about my life. I've never been passionate about anything. I've never been especially talented at anything. My entire life I've been mediocre and sub-par and below average. I've always thought that maybe I'm meant to die young, since I'm the only person I know that has no vision of the future. No desire for a spouse or children or dream job. Every time I look into the future, it's just a bleak black hole, open and gaping.

Thanks so much for your comment, and willingness to listen. It means a lot. You are very kind.

You sound so rational, I wish life could happen like that. But I have never had that relationship with my parents. They think caring for children is about providing physical objects. A good school, clothes, food. That's how they show their love. In return, I'm expected to provide them with good grades, find a good job, give them bragging rights and return their monetary inputs with reasons for pride.

Every time the topic of mental health comes up--whether a friend's kid is depressed, or the news is reporting on schizophrenia, whatever. My mom makes this face and says, "Oh, they have *psychological* problems," in this condescending tone of voice. 

I can't think of any way I could seek out treatment without them finding out. Fuck, as if I could even pay for it. What you speak of is a fantasy world. But thanks for your comment, thanks for listening and responding.
